## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka* (Ja 449) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection. According to the traditional framing preserved in the text, the Buddha delivered this discourse while residing at Jetavana near Sāvatthī, prompted by a landowner who was so overwhelmed by grief after the death of his beloved son that he neglected bathing, eating, work, and attendance on the Buddha [SuttaCentral].
Eugene W. Burlingame observed that the author of the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* reworked the material of Jātaka 449—merging both its introduction and its story of the past into a single unified narrative while expanding it considerably [Burlingame 1921]. He further noted that the conversion of Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī by the Buddha, which forms a central element in the *Dhammapada* commentary and its derivative version in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, is absent from the Jātaka version itself [Burlingame 1921].
SuttaCentral identifies passage-level parallels within the Jātaka collection in the *Sujātajātaka* (Ja 352), *Migapotakajātaka* (Ja 372), *Somadattajātaka* (Ja 410), and *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454), and notes related accounts in the *Petavatthu* (Pv 8, Pv 17, Pv 18, Pv 25) and *Vimānavatthu* (Vv 83) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms these connections, recording 63 matching passages across 11 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. In particular, segments 0.3–10.4 of Ja 449 share extensive verse material with the *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 83) and *Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu* (Pv 17), while verses 7.4–10.4 recur identically or near-identically in *Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 454), *Kaṇhapetavatthu* (Pv 18), *Goṇapetavatthu* (Pv 8), and *Ubbaripetavatthu* (Pv 25), alongside their respective commentaries [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-language matches with Tibetan narrative collections, including the *Jātakamālā* (D4150) and *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155) [DharmaNexus].
